title: Is an Extended Warranty Worth It? A Finance Insider's Numbers
summary: A former dealership finance manager turned buyer-advocate explains dealer markup on extended warranties and when buying coverage elsewhere is worth it.

assertions.quote: The dealership markup on extended warranties ranges from 100% to 400% above wholesale cost
buying directly from a third-party provider or through a manufacturer program after the sale almost always costs significantly less
A $3,000 warranty financed at 7% over 60 months adds approximately $570 in interest
Extended warranties are most valuable on vehicles with complex electronics, known reliability issues, or repair costs that exceed the warranty price.
They are least valuable on highly reliable vehicles with strong factory warranty coverage.

verdicts.note: If expected repairs are cheap and infrequent, the premium (which must exceed expected payout to profit) more easily exceeds the benefit.

Abito & Salant's margin estimates (62-73% across TV subcategories) are consistent with lower-failure-rate items yielding worse value, though the paper studies TVs, not vehicles, and doesn't break margins down specifically by vehicle reliability.

assertions.quote: Most manufacturer-backed plans can be purchased any time before the factory warranty expires.
Most states require a cancellation window (typically 30 to 60 days) during which you can cancel for a full refund.
Some third-party warranties require repairs at specific shops.
